scalars.scalar_value: Any combination equivalent to: college-level coursework in fire technology or a related field, and one year of experience working with fire service training, equipment or fire service instructional support.

items.item_text: Valid California driver's license.
CPR/First Aid/EAD

Any combination equivalent to: college-level coursework in fire technology or a related field, and one year of experience working with fire service training, equipment or fire service instructional support.
Maintain annual fire qualifications to provide field experience into instructional support.
Assists students in classroom, lab, and field training activities, including skill stations and live fire burns. (E)
Assists in the administration of projects, and in the preparation of skill demonstrations. (E)
Supports on and off campus lab exercises under instructor facilitation. (E)
Updates and maintains records of attendance according to established procedures. (E)
Assists with routine reports, training documentation, purchase requests, and supply orders. (E)
Assists students in the use of tools, equipment, PPE, and safety practices. (E)
Distributes and performs inspections and preventative maintenance, cleanliness, and minor repairs on program tools, gear, and equipment. (E)
Orders, tracks, and inventories classroom supplies, PPE, training props and apparatus’. (E)
Coordinates and performs the ordering, receiving, distribution, use, tracking, and disposal of hazardous materials in compliance with District procedures. (E)
Assists in recruiting students during outreach functions. (E)
Assists with supporting program operations by coordinating logistics for training events, drills, and field exercises. (E)
Performs other related duties as may be assigned.
Completion of NWCG S-130: Firefighter Training
Firefighting procedures, training apparatus and equipment uses.
Demonstrate the proper utilization of equipment and materials.
FEMA IS-700: Introduction to the National Incident Management System (NIMS)
Fire service tools, Personal Protection Equipment (PPE), equipment, safety procedures, and training props.
Assist students and instructors in classroom, lab, and field environments.
Inventory methods and recordkeeping practices.
Maintain accurate inventory and training records.
Proper storage, and handling of hazardous materials.
Perform preventative maintenance and minor repairs on fire service equipment.
Technical aspects of fire service training and equipment.
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with students, staff, and external partners.
Basic computer operation, including Microsoft Office and spreadsheet applications.
Transport supplies and equipment from the college to training sites.
Strong organizational and recordkeeping techniques.
Follow written and verbal instructions with attention to detail.
Wildland/structural firefighting equipment.
Lifting and carrying heavy equipment up to 50 pounds.
Standing for extended periods of time.
Bending and reaching.
Working outdoors and in field environments, including heat, smoke, and uneven terrain.
Classroom, lab, and field training environments.
Exposure to heat, smoke, fumes, and hazardous materials.
Working with machinery and equipment with moving parts.
Driving a vehicle to conduct work.
Moderate noise level.
Travel for various off-site meetings, trainings, conferences, and/or events.
Each recruitment is conducted independently from others; therefore, interested parties need to submit separate complete application packages for each position they apply for.
It is important the applicants submit ALL documents requested for the application package to be deemed complete and given consideration.
Application
Current resume
Letter of Intent (Cover Letter)
Copy of Transcripts of all degrees and Supplemental Coursework
All out of the country, transcripts must be evaluated prior to submitting them with applications.
Any evaluation service member of the National Association of Credential Evaluation Service (NACES) http://www.naces.org/ is acceptable.

NWCG S-130: Firefighter Training with hands-on skills and safety, including fire behavior, safety procedures (LCES, 18 Watchouts), hand tools, water handling, fire line construction, PPE, incident command basics, and basic fire suppression tactics.
Maintain knowledge, skills and abilities related to firefighting procedures and equipment.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Dexterity of hands and fingers to operate equipment.
